title: QUORUM read: R = 2 overlaps W = 2, so the newest write is always seen
caption: R + W = 4 > N = 3, so at least one replica in every read set took the latest acknowledged write.

messages.label: read c1 (QUORUM)
messages.note: R = 2: the coordinator needs two answers.

messages.label: value · ts = 98
messages.note: Replica 3 was down during the write and still has the older value.

messages.label: newest ts wins → 105
messages.note: Last write wins, by per-cell timestamp.

messages.label: read repair: ts = 105
messages.note: The coordinator fixes the stale replica in the background, so the next read finds them in agreement.

scenarios.name: Risk: R + W ≤ N
scenarios.summary: With W = 1 and R = 1 the read set can miss the write set entirely: the read returns an old value and reports success.

messages.label: write ts=105
messages.note: Replica 1 acks first, so the write succeeds. Replica 3 hasn't applied it yet.

messages.label: read c1 (ONE)
messages.note: R = 1: one answer is enough, and the coordinator picks replica 3.

messages.label: value (ts = 98)
messages.note: Stale, with no error: nothing in the read set saw the write. Use R + W > N when a read must see the last write.

scenarios.name: Alternative: W=ALL, R=ONE
scenarios.summary: R + W > N also holds with W = 3, R = 1: very cheap consistent reads, but a single replica down makes every write fail.

messages.label: read c1 (ONE)
messages.note: Writes were done at ALL, so every replica has ts = 105.

messages.label: read
messages.note: One replica is enough: any of them has the latest write.

messages.label: value (ts = 105)
messages.note: Half the read work of QUORUM. The cost moved to writes: with W = ALL, one node down and nothing can be written.

scenarios.name: Edge: tombstones
scenarios.summary: Reading past many deletes is slow: a replica scans every tombstone in the slice, and past ~100k cells the query is aborted.

messages.label: read latest 50 of c1
messages.note: c1 is used like a queue: rows are inserted and soon deleted.

messages.label: scan 120k tombstones
messages.note: Each delete left a tombstone, kept until gc_grace (10 days) so it can reach every replica.

messages.label: abort: tombstone limit
messages.note: Past tombstone_failure_threshold the replica gives up.

messages.label: ReadFailure
messages.note: Fix the model, not the timeout: partition by time bucket so old buckets are skipped, or use TTLs on whole partitions.
